comments.body:
Research: Jira-integration deletion semantics (2026-08-10)

Jira itself exposes link deletion as an explicit event and operation, not merely as absence: Cloud webhooks include issuelink_created and issuelink_deleted, and REST deletes a specific issue link by stable linkId. Sources: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/webhooks/#issue-link-webhooks and https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-links/#api-rest-api-3-issuelink-linkid-delete

A maintained OSS comparison is GitHub's ghas-jira-integration (github/ghas-jira-integration, updated 2026-08-03). It embeds a durable alert association key in managed Jira issues, handles explicit jira:issue_deleted webhooks, and stores a per-repository prior-state map in Jira. Its full reconciliation builds the union of known source alerts and associated Jira issues; it deletes only when an issue is proven associated and the authoritative source listing proves the alert absent. Sources: https://github.com/github/ghas-jira-integration/blob/main/sync.py and https://github.com/github/ghas-jira-integration/blob/main/jiralib.py

Comparison: the proposed peer-confirmed marker follows the same essential rule—absence may delete only something previously proven to be synchronized. That is materially safer than treating any missing inbound link as a deletion. However, a boolean peer-confirmed flag is weaker than the established patterns: it does not retain Jira's linkId, which side created the link, which authoritative snapshot confirmed it, or whether the current read was complete and newer than that confirmation.

Recommended refinement: persist a managed-link record keyed by relation+target containing Jira linkId when available, origin/direction, confirmed baseline or snapshot revision, and last-confirmed time. Delete on an explicit issuelink_deleted event; during polling, infer deletion only from a successful authoritative complete snapshot newer than the confirmation. A partial/paginated/failed/stale response must never become deletion evidence. This retains the ticket's peer-confirmation idea but makes the evidence strong enough for bidirectional reconciliation.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Additional maintained-project comparison: softrams/bulwark (~187 stars, updated 2026-06) uses a simpler one-way ownership model. Each vulnerability stores its Jira ID/URL; the integration explicitly creates or updates that known Jira issue and explicitly adds the parent issue link. It does not infer link deletion from absence. Source: https://github.com/softrams/bulwark/blob/master/src/utilities/jira.utility.ts. This avoids the ambiguity entirely but cannot satisfy rebar's bidirectional-deletion requirement. Together with GitHub's stateful GHAS sync, the common pattern is: retain durable association/provenance and perform explicit managed mutations; do not treat an unqualified missing link as deletion.

comments.body:
## Decomposition design calls (2026-08-12, epic driver) — derived from the recorded direction, NOT new scope

Three placement questions the description leaves to implementation. Recording them here so the
children inherit one answer and reviewers can challenge it in one place.

**D1 — Storage home: a `.bridge_state` sidecar, NOT ticket `compiled_state`.**
New module `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/peer_confirmations.py`, store at
`.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/peer_confirmations.json`, modelled on `impossible_links.py`
(SCHEMA_VERSION, `record_key(source, target, relation)`, atomic mkstemp+os.replace save).
Rationale: the record carries the **Jira linkId** and is peer-derived, while
`src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py` is deliberately provider-agnostic (LOCAL ids only, so the
primitive is reusable for Linear/GitHub) — putting vendor link ids into reducer state would
break that and would emit a ticket event (auto-committed + auto-pushed to the `tickets` branch)
on every outbound link push. All other peer-derived state already lives in `.bridge_state`
(bindings.json peer baselines, `peer_parent` via `peer_state.py`).
The description's "survives SNAPSHOT compaction" constraint is satisfied **trivially** by a
sidecar (ticket-log compaction cannot touch it) and S1 asserts it with a behavioral test rather
than inheriting it. **Load-bearing consequence:** the new file MUST be added to the staged
`_rel_files` list in `reconcile_helpers.py::_commit_binding_store_snapshot` or it is lost on
every CI checkout — this is bug b8b1's recorded lesson.

**D2 — Key shape: `(source_local_id, target_local_id, relation)`, relation-scoped.**
Matches the consumer (`_inbound_unlink_one`, relation-scoped since e39f) and the existing
`impossible_links.record_key`. Deliberately NOT the outbound ADD dedup key
`(vendor_type, target_key)`, which is direction-agnostic and explicitly not relation-keyed
(`outbound_links.py::_diff_links` docstring) — that key cannot express the granularity G3 needs.
No translation cost: the outbound ADD payload already carries `relation`, so the dispatch
success point has it in hand.

**D3 — "confirming snapshot revision" == `pass_id`.**
The codebase has no snapshot revision counter, ETag, or monotonic remote version; `pass_id` is
the only handle identifying which fetch confirmed a link. Records therefore store
`confirmed_pass` (the pass id) + `confirmed_at` (epoch ns) rather than an ordered revision.
Ordering-sensitive logic must not be built on it.

Write point for outbound confirmation: `dispatch_one.py::_update_one_dispatch_links`, immediately
after `set_relationship` succeeds (the sole `set_relationship` call site in the engine).
Snapshot-confirmation seam: the persist phase of `reconcile.py`, as a sibling of the existing
`_advance_baselines(binding_store, ctx.curr_snapshot, ...)` call — the established precedent for
"learn peer state from the current snapshot at end of pass".
Completeness signal for S2 already exists and needs no new mechanism:
`fetcher.py::merge_issuelinks_map` writes the `issuelinks` key ONLY on an authoritative read
(absent key == unobserved; `[]` == authoritative-empty), and `BackendPaginationStallError`
re-raises rather than degrading.

comments.body:
## Epic complete — all four children closed, all four changes merged and Verified +1

| Story | Ticket | Gerrit | Merged commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 persist the record | `nonlineal-melancholy-grouper` (248f) | 1672 | `c638bc6947` |
| S2 confirm from snapshots | `soured-elmy-ostrich` (83d3) | 1683 | `3476af3d52` |
| S4 backfill at upgrade | `timeless-elusive-joey` (f6e9) | 1698 | `4a8e6a77ba` |
| S3 decline unconfirmed | `cinematic-untiring-dunnart` (47a0) | 1705 | `4010da6493` |

Every change carried `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` before submit; each was closed only after
its change merged.

## What the epic delivers

The blind spot: `managed_refs` marks a ref managed the instant it is created LOCALLY and is
strictly monotonic, so G3 proved OWNERSHIP, never that the peer had ever seen the link. G4 covered
that only when the outbound differ re-emitted the ADD, and `outbound_links._diff_links` dedups ADDs
direction-agnostically on `(vendor_type, target_key)` — "intentionally NOT deduped on relation" —
so a local `blocks` link colliding with an inward `Blocks` on the same pair was never pushed AND
never G4-protected. Post-e39f its removal record reached the applier and deleted a link the peer
never carried.

The fix follows the pattern both maintained comparisons converge on (GitHub ghas-jira-integration;
contrast softrams/bulwark): retain durable association/provenance and never treat an unqualified
missing link as deletion evidence. A removal is now honoured ONLY for a link some pass positively
proved the peer carries.

## The three acceptance criteria

- A removal record for a managed-but-never-peer-confirmed link is DECLINED and logged, and the
  decline count is surfaced in the per-pass INFO summary (this defect class was silent every time,
  so a silent fix would have repeated it).
- A removal for a peer-confirmed link still CONVERGES, relation-scoped exactly as e39f made it.
- Behavior is covered by behavioral tests through `_inbound_update_apply_links` /
  `compute_inbound_mutations`, never by asserting on logs.

## Design decisions worth carrying forward

- **Sidecar, not reducer state.** The record carries the vendor link id, while `_managed_refs` is
  deliberately provider-agnostic; a `.bridge_state` sidecar also survives ticket-log SNAPSHOT
  compaction structurally and emits no auto-pushed ticket event per link push.
- **Relation-scoped key** `(source_local_id, target_local_id, relation)`, matching the reader —
  NOT the direction-agnostic outbound dedup key, which cannot express that granularity.
- **Completeness is a trichotomy.** Absent `issuelinks` = unobserved, `[]` = authoritatively empty,
  populated = evidence. Consumed from `fetcher.merge_issuelinks_map` rather than reinvented.
  There is deliberately NO un-confirmation path: inferring deletion from absence is the very
  failure this epic removes.
- **One store instance** for the persist-phase evidence step. Two would defeat the same-pass
  provenance upgrade and, worse, race a LOST UPDATE where the later save discards the other's
  records. Pinned by a regression test.
- **Fail-open throughout.** An unopenable/corrupt store disables the decline and restores pre-a4bd
  behaviour; evidence is an optimisation of safety, never a precondition for applying a removal.

## Verification

- New suites: 20 (S1) + 14 (S2) + 13 (S4) + 10 (S3) tests.
- `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` -> 2551 passed at the final tree.
- Full CI-equivalent `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` -> 12504 passed / 60 skipped.
- Mutation checks recorded per story: the `_tracked_basenames` staging guard (S1), the
  no-downgrade skip and the true lost-update arrangement (S4), and the confirmation guard itself
  (S3, killed by four cells including the epic's motivating scenario).
- Five pre-existing cells in `test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` and `test_impossible_links_cicada.py`
  were given confirmation fixtures rather than workarounds — each models a peer that HELD a link and
  then deleted it, which by construction implies it was synchronized.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Ticket e39f-5055-f5af-424a makes the reconciler's inbound link-removal path (G5, apply_inbound_records.py::_inbound_unlink_one) converge by removing exactly the mirrored (target, relation) link. The safety analysis surfaced a PRE-EXISTING blind spot inherited from 2b16's design: managed_refs marks a ref managed the instant it is created LOCALLY (reducer/_managed_refs.py — strictly monotonic), so G3 cannot distinguish a brand-new never-pushed local link from a peer-deleted one. G4 (same-pass outbound-ADD suppression) covers that blind spot ONLY when the outbound differ emits the re-ADD; outbound_links.py::_diff_links dedups ADDs direction-agnostically on (vendor_type, target_key) ('intentionally NOT deduped on relation'), so a local link whose vendor type collides with an existing remote link in the other direction (blocks vs inward Blocks) is never pushed AND not G4-protected — an inbound removal record for it can reach G5 and remove a never-pushed local link. This is order-dependently true TODAY (when the never-pushed link is the pair's most-recent, pair-scoped unlink removes it after G5's relation match passes); e39f makes the outcome order-independent but does not add a discriminator.

## Approach

Design pass: persist enough peer-link history (e.g. record (relation, target) as 'peer-confirmed' only after an outbound link ADD is successfully applied or the link is observed in a fetched snapshot) so _inbound_unlink_one can decline removals of never-peer-confirmed links. Must reconcile with managed_refs monotonicity and compaction (SNAPSHOT restore).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a removal record for a managed-but-never-peer-confirmed link is declined and logged.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -k declines`
- [x] a removal for a peer-confirmed link still converges.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -k converges`
- [x] behavior covered by behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations/_inbound_update_apply_links.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py`
- [x] all four children (S1-S4) are closed and their changes are Verified +1 on Gerrit.
      Proof: `rebar list --parent despotic-floriated-leopard` shows every child `closed`

## Testing

Each child carries its own suite and gate commands; the epic is proven by the union of them:
`make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` green on the final child,
plus the existing `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py`
regression suite staying green throughout.

## Chosen direction (operator-approved 2026-08-12; research comments above are the evidence base)

Follow the pattern both maintained comparisons converge on (GitHub ghas-jira-integration; contrast softrams/bulwark): **retain durable association/provenance and perform explicit managed mutations; never treat an unqualified missing link as deletion evidence.**

Concretely: persist a **full peer-confirmation record** per managed link (Jira linkId, direction, the confirming snapshot revision, confirmed-at time) — not a minimal boolean — because Jira exposes deletion as an explicit event keyed by stable linkId, and the completeness tracking S2 needs is impossible with a boolean. A partial/paginated/failed read is NON-EVIDENCE. Backfill grandfathers existing managed links as confirmed-at-upgrade (marked as such) so the first post-upgrade run does not decline every legitimate removal.

## Decomposition (children)
- S1: define + persist the peer-confirmation record (written on successful outbound link ADD; survives SNAPSHOT compaction; reconciled with managed_refs monotonicity).
- S2: populate confirmations from fetched authoritative snapshots, recording snapshot completeness; partial reads can never confirm nor deny.
- S3: _inbound_unlink_one declines-and-logs removal of never-peer-confirmed links (behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations).
- S4: backfill migration marking existing managed links confirmed-at-upgrade.
compiled_state.title: Discriminate never-pushed managed links from peer deletions in the inbound removal path
